questions.question: A company must label 20,000 short support tickets an hour at the lowest cost, and each label is one of eight fixed categories. Which option should you choose?

options.text: A small language model such as Phi-4-mini-instruct
options.why: Correct. A small model handles narrow, high-volume tasks cheaply and quickly.

options.text: A reasoning model
options.why: A reasoning model costs more and runs slower, and this task needs no multistep thinking.

options.text: An audio-capable model
options.why: The input is text, so audio capability adds nothing.

options.text: Content Understanding
options.why: Content Understanding extracts fields from documents, images, audio and video, not short text labels.

questions.explanation: Choose the smallest model that passes your tests. Narrow, high-volume labelling suits a small language model.

questions.question: An app sends product photos to a deployed model and receives an HTTP 400 error that says image input is not supported. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The deployment has too little quota
options.why: Insufficient quota produces HTTP 429, not a 400 about input type.

options.text: The deployed model accepts text input only
options.why: Correct. Supported input types are listed on the model card, and a text-only model rejects images.

options.text: The guardrail blocked the image
options.why: A guardrail block returns a content filter error, not an unsupported input error.

options.text: The project endpoint is public
options.why: Network exposure does not change which inputs a model accepts.

questions.explanation: Check the model card for supported inputs before you design the solution.

questions.scenario: A finance team receives scanned supplier invoices in varied layouts. It needs vendor name, total and due date as structured fields, with no prompt maintenance.
questions.question: Which Foundry service should you use?

options.text: Azure Speech
options.why: Azure Speech works with audio, not scanned documents.

options.text: A reasoning model with a long prompt
options.why: This works poorly compared with a service built for fields, and it needs prompt maintenance.

options.text: Content Understanding
options.why: Correct. It extracts structured fields from documents without prompt engineering.

options.text: Azure Translator
options.why: Translator converts text between languages and does not extract fields.

questions.explanation: Use a Foundry Tool when the job is fixed and well defined, such as document field extraction.

questions.question: An agent must answer employee questions from 3,000 internal policy documents and return citations. Which Foundry capability should you use to ground the agent?

options.text: A larger model with a longer system prompt
options.why: A longer prompt cannot hold 3,000 documents and gives no reliable citations.

options.text: Global Batch deployment
options.why: Batch is a deployment type for offline work and does not ground answers.

options.text: A small language model fine-tuned on the questions
options.why: Fine-tuning does not provide citations to current documents.

options.text: A Foundry IQ knowledge base on Azure AI Search
options.why: Correct. It returns grounded passages with citations from indexed company content.

questions.explanation: Grounding on company content is done with a knowledge base on Azure AI Search, not a bigger model.

questions.question: You are comparing two models that both appear suitable for a summarisation task. What should drive the final choice?

options.text: The model with the highest public quality index
options.why: A public index averages other tasks and may not predict results on your data.

options.text: Scores from your own test set, together with cost and latency
options.why: Correct. Your data and requirements decide, because public benchmarks may not match your task.

options.text: The model with the largest context window
options.why: Context size matters only if the task needs it.

options.text: The model released most recently
options.why: Release date does not indicate fit for your task.

questions.explanation: Test candidates on real inputs and choose the smallest that meets the bar.
